weeks.label: Week 9
weeks.focus: Transition to marathon training • Build aerobic endurance • Establish marathon pacing and fueling practice
weeks.notes:
MARATHON CONTINGENCY 12-WEEK EXTENSION
WEEK 9
BUILD ENDURANCE. MAINTAIN FORM. STAY HEALTHY. REACH 26.2.

FOCUS:
- Transition to marathon training
- Build aerobic endurance
- Establish marathon pacing and fueling practice

WEEKLY VOLUME: ~25-30 MILES (or time equivalent) + strength, mobility and recovery

LONG RUN: 90-110 MIN Steady aerobic pace (Zone 2)

RUNS THIS WEEK: 3 runs + 1 optional easy run

STRENGTH: 2 sessions (full body, posterior chain and core focus)

DAILY MOBILITY: 5-10 minutes (before and/or after runs)

WEEK 9 GOALS:
- Complete ~25-30 miles (or time equivalent).
- Establish consistent long run (90-110 min).
- Maintain 2 strength sessions.
- Practice fueling and hydration on long run.
- Keep easy runs truly easy (Zone 2).
- Maintain good running form: slight forward lean, high cadence, relaxed shoulders, glutes engaged.
- Stay consistent and injury-free.

NUTRITION & FUELING FOCUS:
DAILY HYDRATION:
- 2.5-4 L water (more in heat).
LONG RUN FUELING:
- Start with 30-60 g carbs per hour.
- Examples: gels, chews, or sports drink.
- Practice what you will use on race day.
DAILY NUTRITION:
- Emphasize complex carbohydrates, lean protein, and healthy fats.
- Include electrolytes, especially on longer runs and in hot conditions.

exercises.name: RUN 1 – EASY RUN (AEROBIC BASE)
howTo: Warm-up: 5-10 min easy jog
Main Run: 45-55 min Zone 2 (RPE 3-4)
Focus: relaxed form, midfoot landing, glutes engaged
Cool down: 5 min easy jog + light stretching
exercises.workoutNote: WEEK 9 RUN SCHEDULE

exercises.name: RUN 2 – INTERVALS + THRESHOLD WORK
howTo: Warm-up: 10-15 min easy jog + dynamic drills
Main Set:
• 4 × 6 min at Zone 4 (comfortably hard pace)
• 2 min easy jog between
Cool down: 10 min easy jog
Focus: smooth form, controlled effort, even pacing

exercises.name: RUN 3 – LONG RUN

Main Run: 90-110 min Zone 2 (conversational pace)
Practice fueling:
• 30-60 g carbs per hour (gels, chews, or drink mix)
• 500-750 ml fluid per hour
Optional: last 10-15 min progress slightly to upper Zone 2
Cool down: 5-10 min easy jog + stretching

exercises.name: OPTIONAL RUN 4 – RECOVERY RUN
howTo: Keep it easy and relaxed
30-40 min Zone 1-2 (RPE 2-3)
Focus on recovery, blood flow, and form
If feeling fatigued, replace with mobility or rest

DAILY NUTRITION:
- Emphasize complex carbohydrates, lean protein, and healthy fats.
- Include fruits, vegetables, and electrolytes to support recovery and adaptation.

weeks.notes:
MARATHON TAPER PLAN
THE FINAL 3 WEEKS
WEEKS 21-23
REST. RECOVER. STAY SHARP. ARRIVE STRONG.
RACE DAY WEEK 23 26.2 MILES.

WEEKLY FOCUS:
- Reduce total volume each week.
- Maintain running economy and form.
- Prioritize sleep, nutrition, and recovery.
- Keep strength work light and purposeful.
- Practice race-day fueling and gear.
- Stay healthy and injury-free.

RECOVERY TOOLS:
- COLD PLUNGE 2-3 min as needed
- SAUNA 10-20 min (not race day)
- FOAM ROLLING 5-10 min daily
- MORILITY Ankle/knee/hip circles + light stretching
- SLEEP 7-9 hours per night

NUTRITION GUIDELINES:
- CARB LOAD 36-48 hours before race (as tolerated)
- HYDRATION Individualize based on climate, sweat rate, and
- FUELING PRACTICE Use what you have trained with (60-90 g carbs/hr)
- SODIUM 500-1000 mg per hour (especially if warm)

KEY REMINDERS:
- No new foods, gear, or supplements.
- Keep all runs easy and controlled.
- Avoid heavy lifting or intense cross-training.
- Focus on sleep, hydration, and stress reduction.
- Trust your training. Execute your plan.
- Enjoy the race!

MDFIT PERFORMANCE & REHAB — BUILD ENDURANCE. MAINTAIN FORM. STAY HEALTHY. REACH 26.2. — GOSD (GLUTES ON. SHOULDERS DOWN.)

sourceNotes: Read 13 sheets (weeks 9-20 main series + taper) downloaded via Drive thumbnail at w2400 (weekly sheets 1024x1536 portrait; taper 1536x1024 landscape), cropped and upscaled 2x. Each weekly sheet: header (MD FIT PERFORMANCE & REHAB / MOVE BETTER. PLAY LONGER. / MARATHON CONTINGENCY / 12-WEEK EXTENSION | WEEK N / BUILD ENDURANCE. MAINTAIN FORM. STAY HEALTHY. REACH 26.2.), a 6-box strip (FOCUS, WEEKLY VOLUME, LONG RUN, RUNS THIS WEEK, STRENGTH, DAILY MOBILITY), a 4-card run schedule (Run 1-3 + Optional Run 4, each with day, duration, zone and WORKOUT DETAILS bullets), STRENGTH TRAINING (2 sessions of 7 numbered exercises, 'name – sets × reps'), DAILY MOBILITY ROUTINE (3 circles + Additional line), WEEK N GOALS and NUTRITION & FUELING FOCUS; all of these are recorded per week (runs/strength/mobility as exercises; header boxes, goals, nutrition and footer in week notes) because they change week to week. Mapping: each run card is one exercise (name = card title verbatim, workout = printed day, dosage.other Duration and Zone/note = the card's time box, howTo = WORKOUT DETAILS bullets in order, sub-bullets prefixed '• '); strength rows -> name/sets/reps with workout = session heading; mobility -> reps. Weeks 9-13 have no bottom footer band; weeks 14-15 footer 'MDFIT — EXPERT CARE. INTEGRATED SERVICES. TEAM THAT KNOWS YOU. ALL INCLUDED.'; weeks 16-20 add the GOSD logo. Weeks 9-13: long run on Sunday, optional run on Saturday; weeks 14-20: long run Saturday, optional run Sunday.
